title: Nonzerodivisors in a flat simultaneous-root tower
statement:
Let $A,R$ be commutative rings and $a:A\to R$ a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $r\geq0$, $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in A$, and $c\in A$ such that multiplication by $c$ is injective on $A$. Let $I$ be a set of positive integers containing $1$, ordered by divisibility, such that every pair in $I$ has a common multiple in $I$. For $n\in I$ put
$$R_n=R[x_{1,n},\ldots,x_{r,n}]/(x_{d,n}^{n}-a(t_d))_{1\leq d\leq r},$$
using polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Give these rings the $R$-algebra transition maps $x_{d,n}\mapsto x_{d,m}^{m/n}$ for $n\mid m$, and let $S=\varinjlim_{n\in I}R_n$ be their ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $Q$ be any commutative $S$-algebra whose structure map $S\to Q$ is flat. Then multiplication by the image of $c$ is injective on $R$, on every $R_n$, on $S$, and on $Q$. No injectivity of the transition maps, characteristic assumption, invertibility of the integers $n$, normality or Noetherian hypothesis is required. The rings $R$ or $Q$ may be zero. For $r=0$ every $R_n=R$ and $S=R$.

source.place: Agent extraction and algebraic generalization of returned Steps 7 and 8: Tag 00HB (algebra-definition-flat), iterated monic polynomial division as used by lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free, and categories.tex Section directed-colimits, eventual-equality description preceding Tag 002W (categories-lemma-directed-commutes). The full tower assertion is an agent assembly of these arguments.

proof.text: The divisibility poset $I$ is small and filtered: it is a subset of the positive integers, contains $1$, and the common-multiple hypothesis supplies upper bounds; parallel arrows in a poset are unique. For $n\mid m$, evaluation sends each relation $x_{d,n}^n-a(t_d)$ to $(x_{d,m}^{m/n})^n-a(t_d)=x_{d,m}^m-a(t_d)=0$, so descends to an $R$-algebra homomorphism $u_{nm}:R_n\to R_m$. For $n\mid m\mid k$, both $u_{mk}u_{nm}$ and $u_{nk}$ fix $R$ and send $x_{d,n}$ to $x_{d,k}^{(k/m)(m/n)}=x_{d,k}^{k/n}$; polynomial evaluation and surjectivity of the quotient map make them equal. The same calculation gives $u_{nn}=\mathrm{id}$. Thus these maps define the stated diagram and its ring-colimit cocone.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), filteredness; polynomial evaluation and quotient definitions

proof.text: Apply lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection over $A$ with flat module $R$ to the injective $A$-linear map $\mu_c:A\to A$, $b\mapsto cb$. Identify $R\otimes_A A$ with $R$ by $r\otimes b\mapsto r a(b)$, with inverse $r\mapsto r\otimes1$. The tensor relations give both inverse identities, and $\mathrm{id}_R\otimes\mu_c$ becomes $r\mapsto a(c)r$. Therefore multiplication by $a(c)$ is injective on $R$.

source.place: Tag 00HB (definition-flat), applied to multiplication; tensor identification from Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: Fix a positive n. Induct on the number r of parameters. For r=0, evaluation into R and the coefficient map are inverse by quotient and polynomial extensionality, so regularity follows from step 2. In the successor step let B be the simultaneous-root quotient for the tail parameters, and let T=B[X]/(X^n-t_0). The polynomial is monic, so lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free makes T free over B, hence flat. Apply the same flat preservation of regularity as in step 2 to the induction hypothesis on B. Define a map f from the full simultaneous-root quotient to T by sending the first variable to the new root and each tail variable to its image from B. All root equations hold, so quotient evaluation gives an R-algebra homomorphism. Conversely the tail roots define B to the full quotient, and adjoining its first root defines g:T to the full quotient. The composite gf fixes every root and coefficient and is the identity by quotient and polynomial extensionality. Thus f is injective; R-linearity transports regularity from T to the full quotient. This proof works also for zero rings and needs no hypothesis on the parameters.

source.place: Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), proof of (10) implies (1), monic quotient finite free; iterated monic-division argument

proof.text: Write $\iota_n:R_n\to S$ for the colimit maps and $c_S$ for the image of $c$. For $z\in S$ with $c_Sz=0$, clause (1) of lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise gives $z=\iota_n(b)$. Thus $\iota_n(c_nb)=\iota_n(0)$, where $c_n$ is the image of $c$ in $R_n$. Clause (2) supplies a stage $m$ and arrows $n\to m$ making the two representatives equal; these arrows coincide because $I$ is a poset. Hence $c_m u_{nm}(b)=0$. Step 3 gives $u_{nm}(b)=0$, and the cocone identity gives $z=\iota_m(u_{nm}(b))=0$. A multiplication map of abelian groups is injective when its kernel is zero, since equal images imply the difference is in the kernel. Therefore multiplication by $c_S$ is injective on $S$. No injectivity of any $u_{nm}$ was used.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual-equality description preceding Tag 002W; Algebra Tags 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit) and 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit)

proof.text: Apply lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection over $S$ with flat module $Q$ to the injective $S$-linear multiplication map $\mu_{c_S}:S\to S$ from step 4. The inverse maps $Q\otimes_S S\to Q$, $q\otimes s\mapsto q s$, and $q\mapsto q\otimes1$ identify this tensor map with multiplication by the image of $c$ on $Q$, exactly as in step 2. It is therefore injective. These arguments allow zero target rings: the unique endomorphism of the zero module is injective. Only positivity of $n$, flatness of the two supplied structure maps and filteredness were used; characteristic, invertibility, normality and Noetherian assumptions are unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 00HB (definition-flat), applied to multiplication; tensor identification from Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: For r=0, define evaluation from each root quotient to R using the empty variable family. Its composite with the coefficient map is the identity by algebra-homomorphism commutation, and the other composite fixes all (empty) variables, hence is the identity by quotient and polynomial extensionality. Thus each coefficient map is bijective. The colimit coefficient map is surjective because each colimit element has a representative at a stage and each stage element is a coefficient. It is injective because equality of the images of two coefficients eventually holds at a later stage; the transition maps preserve coefficients and the later-stage coefficient map is injective. RingEquiv.ofBijective gives the displayed equivalences with exactly the specified coefficient maps.
